kjv: tarried in a place that was far off
mine: they (the king and the people) halted at the last house
note: beit hammerchaq means "the house of the distance", probably the last house of the city before the Kidron, a landmark rather than a vague "far place".

kjv: I (David) will tarry in the plain of the wilderness
mine: I (David) will wait at the fords of the wilderness
note: The ketiv be'avrot ("at the fords") fits David's crossing of the Jordan (17:16). The qere be'arvot ("in the plains") is what the KJV follows. I chose the ketiv.
